transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been thinking a lot about whether my family would be better off if I just weren’t here anymore. My sister and my pastor got really concerned about me and urged me to come get some help. I just feel so tired and lost.
Have you ever had periods lasting several days or more where you felt the exact opposite—unusually happy, full of energy, or needing much less sleep than usual?

Yes, actually. A few months ago, I went through a phase where I felt on top of the world and had this endless energy from dawn until past midnight. I was constantly running around starting new projects and committees, before I eventually crashed into this awful low.
During that period of high energy, did your behavior cause any problems in your daily life or relationships, or did you ever need to be hospitalized because of it?

I wasn't hospitalized, but it caused a terrible strain on my relationships because I was snapping at everyone and getting into arguments over my spending and constant projects. Eventually, I had to cancel all my quilting orders and step down from church committees because I just couldn't manage anything anymore. Now, my sister and friends have to handle my husband's doctor visits and even our household bills.
During this difficult time, have you heard or seen things that others couldn't, or have you had any strong beliefs or fears that others told you weren't true?

No, I've never seen or heard things that weren't actually there. But during that high period, I did truly believe I was destined to turn my small quilting boutique into a huge national brand and single-handedly fix all the historical society's problems, even though everyone else told me I was overreaching and needed to slow down.

During this current low period, have you experienced any strong beliefs that others tell you are unrealistic, such as feeling convinced that you are completely ruined or responsible for some terrible disaster?

Yes, I feel like a terrible wife and mother who doesn't even deserve her family. I constantly blame myself for my husband's health declining, believing all my frantic church projects and business ideas stressed him out and made him sicker. I just lie awake replaying every mistake I've ever made, convinced that I've ruined everything.

When your family or doctors reassure you that your husband's illness is a medical condition and not your fault, are you able to accept that they might be right, or do you remain absolutely convinced that you are to blame?

No matter how much they reassure me, I remain deeply convinced that I am the one to blame. I truly believe that my frantic pushing of all those church projects and business ideas caused the stress that made my husband so sick. I just feel like a terrible wife and mother who doesn't deserve my family at all.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a severe depressive episode characterized by suicidal ideation, profound guilt, and severe functional impairment. She exhibits mood-congruent psychotic symptoms, specifically a delusion of guilt regarding her husband's declining health that remains unshakeable despite reassurance. Additionally, she describes a clear historical manic episode characterized by elevated mood, grandiosity, decreased need for sleep, increased goal-directed activity, and irritability that caused significant interpersonal strain. This combination of a past manic episode and a current severe depressive episode with psychotic features meets the criteria for Bipolar Affective Disorder, current episode severe depression with psychotic symptoms (F31.5).
